**Iteration 3**

**Step 2 \- Establish the Iteration Goal**  
The goal of this iteration is to address architectural concerns in regards to performance, security, and system observability, ensuring the architecture will both safely and reliably support the primary operations of the system. This iteration is focused on refinement of cross-cuttinng structures that were only addressed partially in previous iterations.

Key quality attributes, and concerns that are guiding this iteration include:

QA-1: Performance \- The system should be able to provide quick responses for academic and dashboard data that is commonly accessed.  
QA-2: Availability \- The system should have the ability to be monitored effectively, and keep operating through fault detection.  
QA-4: Security \- Access to sensitive academic information should be consistently protected.

Supporting Drivers

* CON-1: University privacy rules surrounding sensitive academic information  
* CRN-3: Protection, and the proper handling of academic information  
* CRN-5: Real-time health and system metric access

**Step 3 \- Choose One or More Layers to Refine**  
The elements that we will refine in this iteration are modules located in the different layers defined in previous iterations. The selected quality attributes being performance, availability, and security, all globally affect the system causing this iteration to have a focus on refinement of cross cutting components instead of functionality isolated to one layer.

**Step 4 \- Choose One or More Design Concepts that Satisfy the Selected Drivers**

| Design Decision and Location | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Introduce Centralized Security Enforcement Component (Cross-Cutting Layer)** | With security being centralized, a single mechanism can validate all access to sensitive academic data. This directly supports QA-4 (Security), CON-1 (University-wide privacy rules), and CRN-3 (Secure handling of academic information) through prevention of duplicated or inconsistent permission checks across modules. |
| **Implement Unified Logging Pipeline across every module (Cross-Cutting Layer)** | A shared logging structure captures key actions in a format that is consistent (queries, model updates, announcements). This directly supports UC-7 as well as QA-2 through improvement of monitoring of performance issues, failures, and integration errors, It also sets the architecture up for more monitoring and analytics refinements. |
| **Define a system-wide strategy for Error Handling** | Consistent error handling approach leads to predictable behaviour for clients and maintainers by ensuring all modules report failures in the same format. This directly supports CRN-5 as it allows for easier tracking of system health, and reduces complexity of debugging during operational issues. |
| **Introduce Local Caching Rules for the Client Data Layer** | Unnecessary server requests are reduced by specification of when Local Cache must return saved academic or dashboard data. This directly supports QA-1 (performance) via reduction of latency for information that is frequently accessed, and providing more resilience in limited connectivity scenarios. |
| **Define Metrics Collection in the Analytics Store** | Extension of the Analytics Store to collect latency, error rates, and request counts directly supports UC-7, and CRN-5. This further improves system health visibility, also supporting QA-2 (availability) by enabling fast outage detection, and performance degradation. |

**Step 5 \- Instantiate Architectural Elements, Allocate Responsibilities, Define Interfaces**

| Design Decision | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Introduce Centralized Security Enforcement Component (Cross-Cutting Layer)** | The Centralized Security Enforcement Component enforces token validation, role-based access checks, and privacy rules for any sensitive academic operation. Thus, it becomes the single port of enforcement used by every service in order to maintain consistent security behaviour across the whole system. |
| **Implement Unified Logging Pipeline across every module (Cross-Cutting Layer)** | The logging pipeline provides a standard for how modules emit logs, giving a unified structure for recording queries, model updates, announcements, and integration events. This supporting operational monitoring, and simplifying analysis that may arise later. |
| **Define a system-wide strategy for Error Handling** | This strategy defines error objects that are common, return formats, and rules of escalation. It helps ensure failures that occur across modules are consistently handled, nad that error information is both clear and traceable for maintainers. |
| **Introduce Local Caching Rules for the Client Data Layer** | Local Caching Rules specify when either cached academic or dashboard data should be retrieved from the server, or to be returned locally. This improves the response time for information that is frequently accessed, and reduces overall server load. |
| **Define Metrics Collection in the Analytics Store** | The Analytics Store is extended to collect latency, error rate, as well as request count metrics. The metrics with real time system health insight,  as well as support availablilty monitoring. |

| **Sensitivity Points** | **Caching Rules Affect Performance and Freshness** | **Aggressive caching improves performance, but risks returning outdated academic data** |
|  | **Centralized Security Component Latency** | **Every sensitive request goes through the same security gateway, improving security but potentially adding response time overhead.** |
|  | **Unified Logging Volume** | **Heavy logging can introduce system overhead and affect performance if not rate-limite** |
|  | **Metrics Collection Overhead** | **Real-time metric capture improves availability but may increase CPU/IO utilization** |
| **Trade-off Points** | **Security vs. Performance** | **Centralized security strengthens protection, but may slow high-traffic or large-volume data access** |
|  | **Caching vs. Data Freshness** | **Local Caching reduces latency but risks returning stale academic entries.** |
|  | **Logging Detail vs. Runtime Cost** | **Detailed logs support observability but may degrade performance** |
|  | **Redundancy vs. Cost/Complexity** | **Replication and load balancing increase fault tolerance** |
| **Risks** | **Security Implementation Not Yet Technology-Specific** | **Lack of chosen technologies leaves security partially addressed** |
|  | **Logging Backend Not Defined** | **Logging pipeline is designed but not mapped to a concrete log-aggregation technology** |
|  | **Metrics Framework Not Selected** | **Metrics collection plan exists, but no decision on Prometheus, OpenTelemetry etc** |
|  | **Cache Inconsistency Risk** | **Without strong cache invalidation rules, clients may see outdated academic data** |
|  | **Observability Gaps** | **Metrics and logs exist, but without dashboards, operators may still lack timely insight** |
| **Non-Risks (Confirmed Strengths)** | **Uniform Security Enforcement** | **Centralized approach eliminates inconsistent access control across modules** |
|  | **Improved Fault Detection** | **Logging \+ metrics give good system visibility, even without complete tooling choices** |
|  | **Improved Performance for Frequent Access** | **Catching significantly reduces load and latency for commonly accessed dashboard data** |
|  | **Consistent Error Handling** | **System-wide strategy ensures failures behave in a predictable manner** |
